title: Degree-uniform power saving for intersective polynomial differences
exact_target: For each $k>=2$, is there $c_k>0$ such that for every intersective h in Z[x] of degree k with positive leading coefficient, all sufficiently large N and all A subset [N] avoiding nonzero h(t) differences for positive integers t satisfy $|A|<=C_h$ $N^{1-c_k}$, with $C_h$ allowed to depend on h?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
For each $k>=2$, is there $c_k>0$ such that for every intersective h in Z[x] of degree k with positive leading coefficient, all sufficiently large N and all A subset [N] avoiding nonzero h(t) differences for positive integers t satisfy $|A|<=C_h$ $N^{1-c_k}$, with $C_h$ allowed to depend on h?

\subsection{Short English statement}
For each $k>=2$, is there $c_k>0$ such that for every intersective h in Z[x] of degree k with positive leading coefficient, all sufficiently large N and all A subset [N] avoiding nonzero h(t) differences for positive integers t satisfy $|A|<=C_h$ $N^{1-c_k}$, with $C_h$ allowed to depend on h?
